questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code bounds the memory it uses for incoming data? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The intake channel is full because the Run loop is busy with a slow sink. What does a caller of Offer observe, and what does the HTTP client see?
choices: Offer blocks until space frees up, so the HTTP request hangs
Offer returns false immediately and the handler answers 503 with Retry-After, pushing back on the producer
Offer silently discards the event and the handler still answers 202
Offer panics because sending on a full channel is an error

questions.prompt: The sink is down for ten minutes while couriers keep sending at a high rate. How much event data can the Batcher hold in memory in that time?
choices: Unlimited, because failed batches are appended back and the slice grows with every flush attempt
At most the channel capacity, because pending is flushed to disk on failure
At most about queue + maxPending events; beyond that Run counts and drops new ones
Nothing, because a failed flush clears pending to avoid retaining data

questions.prompt: On shutdown, why does Run flush with a context derived from context.Background() rather than reusing ctx?
choices: ctx is already cancelled at that point, so a Write using it would fail immediately and the pending events would be lost
context.Background() makes the flush run faster than a derived context
Using ctx would make the ticker fire again
A cancelled context would panic inside the sink
